correctness.rationale: Part I supplies the Wiman sextic premise Aut(C)=G2(C)≅A6; the modern Wiman-arrangement source supplies the 45 reflection lines and 45 quadruple points. The proof then uses conjugacy of A6 involutions, uniqueness of a projective involution's isolated fixed point, and the exact equivalence P_sigma in ell_tau iff sigma and tau commute. The standalone exact permutation verifier exhausts the 45 involutions, all commuting pairs, all 30 Klein four-groups, and the duad-syntheme incidence model. No finite experiment is used as a substitute for an infinite or geometric theorem.

originality.rationale: The raw Wiman arrangement census is classical and is not claimed as new. The accepted claim is the order-two quasi-Galois identification, the exact center-axis/commutation equivalence, and the resulting Tutte-Coxeter line-graph and two-orbit reflection-triangle structure. The inspected lead, prerequisite, and Wiman-arrangement papers do not state that bridge, and targeted semantic searches returned no implication-equivalent finding.
residual_risks: Older Valentiner/Wiman literature may encode the same pole-mirror incidence or the duad-syntheme model under nineteenth- or early-twentieth-century terminology.

A classical group-theoretic table could record the commuting graph of A6 double transpositions without connecting it to quasi-Galois centers; such a table would cover the abstract finite graph but not automatically the geometric bridge.
The originality assessment is therefore for the combined curve-specific statement, not for the classical Wiman counts or for the abstract existence of the Tutte-Coxeter graph.

value.rationale: The Wiman sextic is a canonical extremal plane curve, and quasi-Galois points were introduced precisely to expose automorphism geometry. Identifying its missing order-two projection-center arrangement with the classical 45-line Wiman configuration and then with GQ(2,2)/Tutte-Coxeter gives a structural dictionary between algebraic projections, reflection geometry, and finite incidence geometry. This is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of the classical line census.
